findings.evidence: template/scripts/_platform_common.py gate_message/gate_failure raise BlockingGateCatalogError, not the exception_type argument. design.md decision 4 and catalog note 11 accept this. The commit also had to copy blocking-gates.toml into tests/test_git_lifecycle.py and tests/test_model_routing.py fixtures, which shows scripts now depend on the catalog being present beside them. Any caller that catches SharedWorkspaceError, RoutingError, HardScopeOverlap or TaskFreshnessError and prints a clean message would instead surface a traceback or a different exit path when the catalog is absent. It still fails closed, but the exit condition is no longer identical.
findings.summary: A missing or malformed catalog makes a gate raise BlockingGateCatalogError (a RuntimeError) in place of the exception type the gate used to raise. Callers that catch the specific type would no longer handle the failure.

findings.evidence: tests/test_blocking_gates.py: test_every_acceptance_test_resolves_to_a_real_test uses resolve_test_id (AST), and test_every_acceptance_test_module_belongs_to_a_test_group checks group membership. Neither executes the named tests. Whether a named test passes therefore depends on the whole-suite run, not on the catalog binding. The weaker guarantee is acceptable but does not match the design wording.
findings.summary: design.md decision 3 says a platform test 'resolves and runs' the acceptance tests listed in the catalog. The new test only resolves them by AST lookup and checks that their module is in a test group.
